title: Rebuild the Oldhand website for the 2.0 pack

rows.title: The conductor skill text and its hard stops come from the imported SKILL.md
rows.observed: Opened http://localhost:4180/ in a new tab at 1440x900 (innerWidth 1440, innerHeight 900). 1) 'What it will not do' has an <ol> with 10 items. I joined the page's item texts and the '## Hard stops' items of skills/oldhand/SKILL.md (both whitespace-collapsed, backticks removed) and hashed them: both give SHA-256 516d6fc4...ae4f, so all 10 items are equal and in the same order. 2) Under 'The skill' the <pre class=skill> block starts with '---' then 'name: oldhand' and ends with 'contract -> trace -> rca -> research -> plan -> build -> review -> qa -> ship -> learn'. Its text is 13192 bytes with SHA-256 fcaf1122...ff55, byte-identical to the 13192-byte SKILL.md (same hash from shasum). 3) The only link in that section, 'View on GitHub', has href https://github.com/berwinsingh/oldhand/blob/main/skills/oldhand/SKILL.md, an exact match (not clicked). 4) A control labelled 'Copy raw' (aria-label 'Copy the whole SKILL.md') sits above the block. Four real clicks each changed its text to 'Copied' for about 1.6 s and then back to 'Copy raw' (logged with a MutationObserver; one screenshot caught 'Copied'). After the clicks the system clipboard was 13192 bytes with the same SHA-256 as SKILL.md. Console had only vite and React DevTools debug/info lines; all 18 requests were 200.

rows.title: Each install tab shows commands, a tested line and the line to type afterwards, and Copy copies the exact command
rows.observed: Opened http://localhost:4180/ in a new tab at 1440x900. The install switcher (tablist 'Install route') has four tabs labelled Any agent, Claude Code plugin, Codex plugin, Git clone; exactly one had aria-selected=true each time I read the DOM (Any agent on load). I clicked each tab and read the panel. Any agent: 1 command block (npx skills add berwinsingh/oldhand --skill '*' -g), a note, three 'Then, in ...' lines (/oldhand ..., $oldhand ..., 'Use the oldhand skill: ...') and 'Tested 2026-10-11 on macOS with skills 1.7.2 ...'. Claude Code plugin: 2 command blocks (/plugin marketplace add berwinsingh/oldhand and /plugin install oldhand@oldhand), a note, 'Then, in Claude Code' with /oldhand:oldhand ..., 'Tested 2026-10-11 with Claude Code 2.1.274 ...'. Codex plugin: 1 two-line block (codex plugin marketplace add berwinsingh/oldhand newline codex plugin add oldhand@oldhand), a note, 'Then, in Codex' with $oldhand ..., 'Tested 2026-10-11 with Codex CLI 0.146.0 ...'. Git clone: 1 three-line block, a note, two 'Then, in ...' lines (/oldhand ... and $oldhand ...), 'Tested 2026-10-11 on macOS with git 2.55.0 and zsh 5.9 ...'. On each tab I added the copy listener, did a real click on the first block's Copy button, and read window.__copied: it was identical (===) to the block's text on all four tabs, including the newline(s) for the 2-line Codex block (81 chars, contains \n) and the 3-line Git block, and the control text read 'Copied' straight after each click. I also copied Claude Code block 2: identical too. navigator.clipboard.readText() was denied (Read permission denied), so the selection-based copy path is what was verified; window.__copied was non-empty every time. ArrowRight with focus on Any agent moved the selection (and focus) to Claude Code plugin; further presses went Codex plugin, Git clone, then wrapped to Any agent.

rows.title: Readable in light and dark at 1440 and 375 with no horizontal scroll, no text under 13px, AA contrast
rows.observed: Used the Browser pane tab-1 (a new tab was refused because the pane was at its tab cap, so I reused a leftover tab after clearing its localStorage, sessionStorage and the two _ga cookies for localhost). For each of four combinations I set the viewport and colour scheme, loaded http://localhost:4180/ fresh, ran an in-page script, then took a screenshot. 1) 1440x900 light: documentElement.scrollWidth 1440 = innerWidth 1440; no visible text element under 13px (smallest 13.5px); body text #1b1b18 on #fbfaf7 = 16.54:1; main links #b4441c on #fbfaf7 = 5.32:1 (hosts.md link on its panel #f2f0ea = 4.87:1); nav links 16.54:1; selected tab 'Any agent' text #1b1b18 = 16.54:1 against the page background (15.15:1 against its own panel #f2f0ea). 2) 1440x900 dark: 1440 = 1440; nothing under 13px (smallest 13.5px); body #ecebe6 on #141413 = 15.44:1; main links #f08a5d = 7.46:1 (hosts.md on panel #1d1d1b = 6.83:1); selected tab 15.44:1 vs page (14.14:1 vs panel). 3) mobile 375x812 light (Pixel UA, 2x): scrollWidth 375 = innerWidth 375; nothing under 13px; same colour pairs and ratios as desktop light (16.54, 5.32, 4.87, 16.54). 4) mobile 375x812 dark: 375 = 375; nothing under 13px; ratios as desktop dark (15.44, 7.46, 6.83, 15.44). A wider scan of every visible text element found zero below AA (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text) at all four combinations; the lowest ratio on the page is 4.87:1. Document text is identical at all four (22859 characters, same hash, same h1, same six h2s, 35 links), so the screenshots show the same content; text in all four screenshots is legible. At 375 wide 40 visible elements extend past the viewport edge, but every one sits inside an intentional overflow-x:auto scroller (header nav, install tablist, npx code block, proof-table wrapper); html and body overflow-x are visible, so the equal scrollWidth is real. Viewport reset to desktop at the end.

rows.title: Analytics stay off until the footer toggle is used; the choice persists; no overlay
rows.observed: Starting state: the Browser pane tab held a leftover 'denied' consent value from an earlier run, so I ran localStorage.clear() on http://localhost:4180 and loaded the entry URL again; localStorage.getItem('oldhand-analytics-consent') === null was true. Step 1: !!document.querySelector('script[data-oldhand-analytics]') was false, no script src or Resource Timing entry contained googletagmanager (the pane's network log also showed none), window.gtag and window.dataLayer were undefined. Step 2: no position:fixed element existed, the only sticky element was the header (HEADER.top), 'Allow analytics' and 'No thanks' were absent from the page text, and there were 0 dialog elements. Step 3: the footer read 'Google Analytics is off; nothing is sent.' with a 'Turn on Google Analytics' button and a 'How Google uses data' link (to https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites). I clicked the button with a real mouse click. Step 4: the footer read 'Google Analytics is on.' with a 'Turn it off' button; localStorage held 'granted'; script[data-oldhand-analytics] existed in <head> with src https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-75YW6HE9FT; Resource Timing listed that gtag/js request plus a www.google-analytics.com/g/collect beacon for tid G-75YW6HE9FT; window.gtag was a function and window.google_tag_manager had the key G-75YW6HE9FT. Step 5: after a fresh navigation and then a literal location.reload() (navigation type 'reload'), with no click, the script element was present again, localStorage was still 'granted', the gtag/js request was in Resource Timing, and the footer still read 'Google Analytics is on.' with 'Turn it off'. Step 6: I clicked 'Turn it off'; localStorage held 'denied' and the footer read 'Google Analytics is off; nothing is sent.' with the 'Turn on Google Analytics' button again. Extra: a reload after turning off showed no script element and no googletagmanager request (consent 'denied').

A second build gave the same bundle hash. 2) Read site/src/App.jsx. REPO is https://github.com/berwinsingh/oldhand (line 9) and BLOB is REPO plus /blob/main/ (line 10). rows.title: The social-preview hook renders the hero inside 1200x627 with no footer or nav
rows.observed: Step 1: opened http://localhost:4180/?social-preview=1 in a fresh headless Chrome (isolated temp profile) with the viewport emulated at exactly 1200x627, device scale factor 1, prefers-color-scheme light (page confirmed innerWidth 1200, innerHeight 627, matchMedia light=true, dark=false). Step 2: in the page, document.documentElement.classList.contains('social-preview') returned true (html class is exactly 'social-preview'); getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('footer')).display returned 'none'; getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.top nav')).display returned 'none'; the first command block (.command, text 'npx skills add berwinsingh/oldhand --skill '*' -g') had getBoundingClientRect().bottom = 470.83, which is within 627. The H1 spans y 104 to 159, the lede 175 to 327, the install panel 355 to 500. The .note, .then and .tested elements are also display none. Step 3: screenshot saved at 1200x627; it shows the wordmark and version line, the H1 'A definition of done for coding agents.', the full four-line-plus lede sentence, the install tabs and the first command block with its Copy button, all uncut. The only thing cut is the 'How it works' heading at the very bottom edge, which is below the first command as allowed. No footer or nav links appear. Viewport override was cleared afterwards (window returned to the headless default 756x469).

rows.title: The analytics regression check passes and guards the opt-in rule
rows.observed: Step 1: ran npm test from /Users/berwinsingh/Documents/oldhand/site (node_modules present). Output: tests 10, pass 10, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0, todo 0, exit code 0, no stderr. grep of test() calls shows 5 in tests/analytics.test.mjs and 5 in tests/slices.test.mjs, matching the order in the output. Step 2: src/analytics.js defines loadAnalytics at line 23. Its only call site in the site tree (excluding node_modules and dist) is line 59, inside applyAnalyticsChoice, guarded by choice === 'granted'. The other branch of applyAnalyticsChoice only calls gtag consent update, and only if gtag already exists and the choice is 'denied'. No other file in src, scripts, public, worker or tests calls loadAnalytics; the tests import no loadAnalytics; index.html contains no GA snippet (only the module script /src/main.jsx). Step 3: src/App.jsx seeds state with useState(readAnalyticsChoice) at line 201 and calls applyAnalyticsChoice(analytics) in a useEffect on mount and on change (lines 202-204). The literal text applyAnalyticsChoice(readAnalyticsChoice()) does not appear verbatim, but the behaviour is equivalent. saveAnalyticsChoice runs only on the footer toggle click (line 208), never on load. The App is not run in a browser; this is a CLI surface, so checks 2 and 3 rest on source reading.

rows.title: A bogus ?agent= value and a blocked localStorage do not break the switcher
rows.observed: Ran in a fresh, isolated Chrome context (Playwright, channel chrome, new context with empty storage) against http://localhost:4180. Step 1: opened /?agent=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C/script%3E. The first tab 'Any agent' was selected (aria-selected=true, class is-active), panel-any was shown, no dialog event fired, no <script> containing alert(1) exists in document.scripts or body HTML, localStorage/sessionStorage were empty, console had only vite debug lines and the React DevTools info line. Step 2: /?agent=codex selected 'Codex plugin' (tab-codex, panel-codex shown). Then a plain http://localhost:4180/ load in the same context selected 'Any agent' again; localStorage and sessionStorage were both {} after the codex visit and after the plain visit, so nothing is stored between visits. Step 3: ran Object.defineProperty(window,'localStorage',{get(){throw new Error('blocked')}}); a direct read confirmed it throws 'blocked'. Clicking 'Git clone' switched to the Git clone tab and panel-git; clicking 'Any agent' switched back to Any agent and panel-any. Step 4: the console after each step showed no errors, no warnings and no pageerror events; no dialogs; no failed requests or 4xx/5xx responses.

rows.title: Zoomed to 200 percent on a phone the page still has no horizontal scroll
rows.observed: Step 1: Browser pane tab-6 set to the mobile preset (375x812, Android UA, DPR 2) and http://localhost:4180/ opened. Before the hack: innerWidth 375, clientWidth 375, scrollWidth 375. Step 2: ran document.documentElement.style.fontSize = '200%'; document.body.style.zoom = '2'. After it: innerWidth 375, clientWidth 375, scrollWidth 375 (bodyScrollWidth 188, x2 zoom = 376), so scrollWidth minus innerWidth = 0. Sideways page scroll attempts all failed to move the page (scrollTo 50/100 left scrollX at 0, a full vertical sweep never saw scrollWidth above 375, a real mouse-wheel scroll right left scrollX at 0); html and body overflow-x are visible, so nothing is hidden by a root overflow rule. 89 element boxes have a right edge more than 1px past 375; every one has an overflow-x:auto ancestor and none lacks one: header nav (4), install tab strip div.tabs (3), install command pre (1), criteria table div.scroll in #example (39), models table div.scroll in #models (42). Each of those five containers itself ends at x<=343 and is genuinely scrollable (scrollWidth > clientWidth: 411/156, 468/154, 440/120, 399/156, 371/156). Text-node scan: 269 text nodes, 69 reach past the screen and all are inside those containers, 0 outside. No element has overflow hidden/clip with hidden content and no text-overflow ellipsis clipping. The h1 'A definition of done for coding agents.' (the failure point in earlier runs) now has overflow-wrap:anywhere, right edge 343, and breaks the word as 'defin' / 'ition' inside the screen; footer nav (flex-wrap: wrap) and p.computed (overflow-wrap:anywhere) also end at 343. Step 3: scrolled to the install block; the command pre scrolls inside itself (scrollLeft 0 -> 320 = max, start 'npx skills ac', end "-skill '*' -g"), page scrollX stayed 0. Clicked through all four install tabs: Any agent 440/120, Claude Code plugin 389/120 and 288/120, Codex plugin 431/120, Git clone 876/120, each pre overflow-x:auto and each end reachable, documentElement.scrollWidth stayed 375 on every tab. Criteria table (Example run, 5 columns): wrapper 399/156 scrolled to its max 243, last columns 'pass' and 'qa:worker' (status, by) visible, page scrollX 0. Step 4: viewport reset to desktop (preset desktop) and page reloaded: innerWidth 1024, scrollWidth 1024, no inline font-size or zoom, desktop UA, 0 touch points. All three expectations held; each has its own evidence file.
